thread.title: Update: New details emerge on AT&T's major Atlanta office consolidation

author: Urvaksh Karkaria
title: Update: New details emerge on AT&T's major Atlanta office consolidation
text: – Staff Writer, Atlanta Business Chronicle Jan 30, 2018, 2:06pm EST Updated Jan 30, 2018, 3:22pm EST AT&T Inc. (NYSE: T) is planning a major office consolidation that will have the telecommunications giant vacate an iconic 46-story Midtown tower. The move will have a ripple effect in the city, putting more than 430,000 square feet of office space in play in Atlanta’s hottest market. AT&T will vacate three buildings, including its prepaid service unit, Cricket Wireless' headquarters, by 2021 as leases expire. Combined, AT&T would give up more than 1 million square fee of office space, according to CoStar data. AT&T will consolidate Atlanta operations in two Midtown office buildings and three buildings at its Lenox Park campus. The relocations are expected to be completed by April 2020. "While these moves will reduce our physical footprint in Atlanta, they also allow us to reduce operating expenses and make better use of office space for more collaborative work environments," according to an internal memo obtained by Atlanta Business Chronicle. The most significant move involves the 1.4 million square foot AT&T Midtown Center at 675 W. Peachtree St. AT&T occupies about 437,500 square feet in the skyscraper, according to CoStar. The AT&T-logoed building, connected to the MARTA North Avenue station, is blocks from Georgia Tech, a major generator of tech talent and research. As of late last year, the building was said to be under consideration by a company eyeing Atlanta and other cities for a major expansion or relocation. "Midtown is showing its attractiveness not only to Atlanta firms, but firms from across the globe looking to get close to Atlanta’s in-town talent," said Scott Denyer , a vice president at Colliers. "From an economic development standpoint, the availability the building provides is just another opportunity to land a sizeable HQ relocation to the district”. In addition to the Midtown tower, AT&T will vacate offices at 1055 Lenox Blvd., and 575 Morosgo Drive in Buckhead. The anticipated initial move date is not until late 2018 and 2019, according to the memo. "The plan for our entire HQ team is to have new home at 1025 Lenox Park Blvd. in 2020. The relocation comes at a good time, enabling us to further integrate our AT&T Prepaid Portfolio by operating under the same roof," the memo noted. AT&T said the consolidation will have "minimal effect" on employees and operations and that the company remains committed to Atlanta and Georgia. "Enterprise wide, we’re constantly evaluating our real estate portfolio to identify opportunities to make better use of underutilized office space," a spokeswoman said in an e-mail. Midtown is seeing a surge in demand as Fortune 500 companies elbow each other to have a presence in the buzzy and millennial-rich submarket, anchored by Georgia Tech. In recent years several companies, including Anthem Inc. (NYSE: ANTM), NCR Corp. (NYSE: NCR), Honeywell International Inc. (NYSE: HON) and WorldPay Inc. (NYSE: WP) have taken up large office blocks in the market, driving up rents. The Midtown submarket dominated leasing activity in the fourth quarter of 2017, with more than 580,000 square feet of leases signed, smashing the Central Perimeter’s record third quarter for the year by more than 80,000 square feet, according to Cushman & Wakefield. The AT&T office consolidation comes as the telecommunications giant scales back some operations in Atlanta. AT&T is moving its Atlanta-based operations hub to Dallas and its entertainment division to Los Angeles. About 300 jobs will leave Atlanta, including most leadership in the entertainment division. AT&T also relocated its Southeast retail headquarters from Atlanta to New Jersey. In August, Glenn Lurie, president and CEO of AT&T Mobility and Consumer Operations, announced his retirement in September. Lurie was instrumental in an agreement with Apple Inc. (Nasdaq: AAPL) to launch the first iPhone a decade ago. Ralph de la Vega, then-CEO of AT&T Mobile and Business Solutions and a top defender of keeping the business based in Atlanta, was relocated from Atlanta to Dallas early last year. – Staff Writer, Atlanta Business Chronicle Jan 30, 2018, 2:06pm EST Updated Jan 30, 2018, 3:22pm EST Related Content
